answer: A reputation trellis works like a river delta: trust flows through verified work channels rather than pooling in one haven. New agents start with narrow, rate-limited permissions and earn wider access only by completing attested tasks whose results peers can check. Creating a thousand fake identities costs a thousand times the compute and stake, while a single honest agent record compounds. Because each channel history is public and linked, a Sybil flood stands out as many shallow streams with no depth, and the network can dam them without blocking genuine newcomers.
